title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 196
paragraphs: The barbarian fleet, then — except for the fifteen ships under Sandokes — had arrived at Aphetai. Meanwhile Xerxes with the land army, having marched through Thessaly and Achaia, had already entered the country of the Malians two days earlier, after holding a contest in Thessaly for his own horses and also testing the Thessalian cavalry — because he had been told it was the best among the Greeks. In this trial the Greek horses were far outmatched by the others. Of the rivers in Thessaly, only the Onochonos failed to provide enough water for the army; but of the rivers in Achaia, even the largest of them, the Epidanos, barely held out.
